newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. Eximbank funds exports for Qatar projects.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Eximbank funds exports for Qatar projects.

text.p: The U.S. Export-Import Bank (Eximbank) has approved $526 million to finance the sale of American equipment and services for two major gas projects in Qatar, the United States Information Service said on Saturday.

A USIS statement said Eximbank approved "$464 million in financing U.S. exports" to Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas Co (Rasgas) to build, own and operate offshore and onshore facilities at the North field.
The bank also approved $62 million to back the sale of American equipment and services for the upstream part of the Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas).
Rasgas in December said it had concluded arrangements for $2.55 billion in loans and bonds to finance a $3.4 billion LNG project.
Rasgas is one of the oil and gas-rich Gulf Arab state's three major gas export projects designed to exploit its mammoth gas reserves -- the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's.
It is 66.5 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation, 26.5 percent by the United States' Mobil Corp, four percent by Japan's Nissho Iwai and three percent by Itochu Corp.

The Rasgas project is scheduled to go onstream in July 1999. Rasgas has signed a 25-year sales and purchase agreement with South Korea's Korean Gas Corporation to supply 2.4 million tonnes of LNG annually from mid-1999 and is negotiating further deals with other customers in the Far East and Asia.
Qatargas went onstream in September of 1996.
